title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 28 (Offer of Sale of Shares by Certain Members of Company)

content.overview: Section 28 allows certain members, in consultation with the Board, to offer all or part of their shareholding to the public in accordance with the prescribed procedure. The offer document is treated as a prospectus of the company for the application of prospectus provisions, with specified adaptations.
content.glance: Member offer for sale in consultation with the Board; offer document treated as company prospectus.
content.study: Where certain members propose to offer all or part of their holding to the public, they may do so in consultation with the Board in the manner prescribed. The document by which the offer of sale is made is deemed to be a prospectus issued by the company, and prospectus enactments apply with the adaptations in the section. The company may pay the expenses of the offer subject to the conditions in the section. Current-law framing: distinguish company primary issue (ss. 23, 26) from secondary offer by members under s. 28; still apply prospectus discipline.

sections.heading: Member Offer for Sale
sections.body: Specified members may offer whole or part of their holding to the public in consultation with the Board, in the prescribed manner.

sections.heading: Offer Document as Prospectus
sections.body: The offer document is deemed a prospectus of the company; prospectus law applies with statutory adaptations.

sections.heading: Expenses
sections.body: The company may pay the expenses of the offer subject to the conditions in the section.

provisions.title: Offer of sale of shares by certain members of company

examples.title: Promoter secondary sale
examples.body: Existing members offer part of their holding to the public in consultation with the Board under the prescribed procedure. The offer document is treated as a prospectus under s. 28.

examples.title: Offer without Board consultation
examples.body: Members attempt a public offer of their shares without Board consultation. Section 28 is not satisfied.

hypotheticals.question: Is a member offer for sale free of prospectus rules?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 28 deems the offer document a prospectus and applies prospectus enactments with adaptations.

misconceptions.correction: Section 28 deems the offer document a prospectus and applies prospectus law with adaptations.

cases.name: Salomon v. A. Salomon & Co. Ltd.
cases.facts: Properly incorporated company challenged as indistinct from controller.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Registered company is a separate legal person.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 28 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Identify member offer and Board consultation. II. Apply prescribed procedure. III. Treat offer document as deemed prospectus. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.answer: Member status; Board consultation; procedure; prospectus compliance; precise relief.
